w4oeha:289: Traditional kernel development requires engineers to master three layers of knowledge simultaneously: hardware architecture constraints (partition dimensions, memory hierarchy), programming model (NKI API semantics), and performance engineering (profiling + optimization loops). The intersection of these three layers is extremely small, resulting in a scarcity of engineers who can write high-performance kernels. The core insight of Neuron Agentic Development is to encode these three layers of knowledge as Agent Skills—hardware constraints are embedded in the writing skill's tiling strategy, API semantics are encoded in the docs skill, and performance engineering is proceduralized as a combination of profiling + querying skills. This allows ML engineers to focus on "what I want to implement" rather than "how the hardware constrains me."
